subject: Transatlantic rate exception & invoicing for residency adders
messages:
From: Helga Bjornsen <helga@nordiccloud.no>
To: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@finserve.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T09:05:00Z
Subject: Initial: hosted API rates + EU residency adders

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo earlier — FinServe liked the latency profile and the routing controls. Procurement asked me to get concrete pricing so we can compare line items against our current vendor. Two specific asks:

- Can you send your hosted-API baseline ratecard (per-token generation + embeddings) for Q3?
- How do you apply data residency adders for EU-hosted workloads? We need to know whether it is a flat percentage, a per-token adder, whether it's applied per region, and whether the charge can be consolidated on a single invoice (we prefer fewer line items).

Also: we expect spiky traffic around month-end settlement windows and we'd like to understand any enterprise discounts or committed-usage pricing you offer.

Appreciate a quick turnaround — procurement is hoping for numbers by end of week.

Best,
Helga
Head of Cloud Partnerships
NordicCloud AS


From: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>
To: Helga Bjornsen <helga@nordiccloud.no>, Procurement Team <procurement@finserve.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-06-07T13:28:00Z
Subject: Re: Initial: hosted API rates + EU residency adders

Hi Helga,

Thanks — glad the demo landed. I attached our Q3 ratecard and the DPA for review (see attachments). High-level answers up front:

- Baseline: Our hosted API list rates are in Redwood_Ratecard_Q3_2027.xlsx (tab: Hosted API). Example baseline generation: $0.0019 / token for standard models, embeddings $0.0006 / vector (per 1k).
- EU residency adder: For hosted deployments where tokens or logs are stored/processed in EU regions we apply a region-specific residency adder. Standard approach: +12% of token charges for EU-hosted requests. This is applied per billing line (so it shows as a separate line item by region on the invoice).
- Exceptions & consolidation: We can offer a consolidated invoice (single invoice with residency lines rolled up) for customers on annual committed agreements; for customers on month-to-month usage the adder typically appears per-region.

Options we can propose to reduce the effective adder:
1) Committed discount: 12-month commit at a committed throughput tier => we can reduce the residency adder to +6% and give a 7% off list on tokens.
2) Volume-triggered waiver: for the first three months after go-live we can waive the residency adder up to a throughput threshold tied to your onboarding plan.
3) Private/Dedicated: If you prefer no residency adder we can evaluate Redwood Dedicated or a Private deployment (different commercial path).

Next steps: if procurement can share target committed spend bands (monthly TU/requests), Marcus and Laura and I will put together a priced mutual-action plan and a clean consolidated invoice structure for your AP.

Attachments: Redwood_Ratecard_Q3_2027.xlsx (xls), DPA_v3.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
+1 (415) 555-0186


From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>

Date: 2027-06-08T09:10:00Z
Subject: Fwd: Initial: hosted API rates + EU residency adders — pricing proposal draft

Tessa / Laura —

Forwarding Helga's request and Tessa's draft responses. Suggested commercial play to make this competitive vs. incumbent:

Proposal (for internal alignment):
- Term: 12-month commitment (FIN-78912).
- Baseline token price: negotiate to $0.0017 / token (10% list reduction).
- Residency adder: reduce to +6% on token line if commit >= $120k/month net of discounts; otherwise +9%.
- Invoice structure: offer batched invoicing for residency charges — single consolidated residency line per month (instead of per-region lines) if customer accepts SAP-friendly PO terms and quarterly remittance.
- One-time onboarding credit: waive residency adder for first 60 days up to 250M tokens.

Risks/notes: legal will need to confirm consolidated invoicing is acceptable for EU VAT/withholding norms. Laura — please confirm with finance whether we can present consolidated monthly residency lines and still meet tax tagging requirements.

Marcus Lin
Pricing Lead, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Marcus / team —

Finance has looked at the consolidated invoice ask. We can offer a batched monthly residency line as long as the customer provides an AP contact and PO terms that include EU tax attributes. We'll need:
- Procurement-signed PO referencing the consolidated billing approach;
- Customer VAT ID (for correct VAT handling);
- An explicit line in SOW that the residency adder is a pass-through fee applied to EU-hosted usage and will be represented as a single line item for month-to-month reconciliation.

Also confirming we can operationalize the onboarding credit (60 days / 250M tokens) but that needs to be tracked via our billing tags; we should add that as a Billing Addendum.

Subject: Re: Initial: hosted API rates + EU residency adders — commercial exception

Helga / FinServe procurement —

Appreciate the thorough questions. We're prepared to make an introductory commercial exception to accelerate your evaluation:

- Offer: 12-month commitment (FIN-78912) at the following commercial terms if signed by 2027-06-30:
  * Token price: $0.00165 / token (effective ~13% off list)
  * Residency adder: +6% (applied as a single monthly residency line if PO includes VAT ID and consolidated-billing clause)
  * Onboarding credit: residency adder waived for first 60 days up to 300M tokens
  * Billing cadence: monthly usage invoice; residency charges batched as one monthly line; quarterly consolidated statements available upon request

- Compliance note: This exception applies to hosted API in EU regions. If you later move to a Private deployment, residency adder will be re-assessed under a separate contract (typical outcome: different billing model).

Next steps: Tessa — please attach a short SOW and updated ratecard reflecting the exception. Helga — if procurement agrees, send PO to procurement@redwood.com and copy legal@finserve.com. We'll circulate a DocuSign for signature.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
VP Sales, EMEA
Redwood Inference
